Welcome to TLC - The Learning Centre
Join Our School
What We Offer
TLC The Learning Centre offers the opportunity to work towards GCSE, Functional Skills and Entry Level qualifications.
TLC The Learning Centre provide a daily nutritious and delicious choice of breakfast and snacks to support good dietary health for all learners. Learners bring their own packed lunches.
TLC The Learning Centre liaises with Local Authorities to support transport applications for our learners.
TLC The Learning Centre supports learners holistically to develop the vital skills needed for lifelong success.
Learners at TLC participate in a broad range of vocational pathways and programmes to help them gain skills for life.
At TLC, we utilise local community resources to offer educational and reward trips and visits.
Testimonials
TLC genuinely care about each and every student and are very understanding to all needs no matter how complex they might be.
As a parent, I cannot recommend this school highly enough. After viewing 18 other settings, the TLC could cater both educational needs as well as emotional and mental.
As soon as I walked in to TLC I knew that it was the right place for my daughter. There was a welcoming environment. It was small and not at all overwhelming. The staff were warm and friendly, the young people said hello to me and I could really feel a sense of community.
My daughter joined TLC 2 years ago. When she first started there she was extremely anxious and traumatised from being in a mainstream school environment. She was so frightened of going to school, but on the first day the whole school looked after her and showed her that it will be OK, that school can be an enjoyable experience. I remember Bella coming home from school that day absolutely buzzing that the other children were nice to her and wanted to include her in the activities they were doing.
My daughter has been attending TLC since year eight. She arrived after a very traumatic year in mainstream secondary which had really knocked her confidence and given her a very low opinion of herself. She very rapidly gained in confidence and self-esteem due to the hard work and support of staff at the school. I would unreservedly recommend TLC to any parent of a child with anxiety and/or learning needs.
I fought for ten years to get my daughter into a school that was suitable for her and TLC The Learning Centre is that school. My daughter has been at this school for two years now and has become a valued member of the school community. Being accepted for who she is has made a huge difference with her confidence and self worth. She has progressed with her education in leaps and bounds, has matured and is a happy teen with where she is at now.
Since my daughter has joined The Learning Centre, she has blossomed, her confidence has grown enormously and she is smashing her goals. Before joining The Learning Centre, she was shy, she had awful panic attacks from the trauma she suffered in mainstream school and she was so far behind in her education, as she was failed by her previous school.
I’m so grateful how all the staff at TLC treat my son – they go above and beyond to help your child. They are all so caring funny and understand their needs. My child LOVES coming here and I appreciate all the hard work and dedication they put in daily for them all.
The staff give such personal care for my child, always helping her feel secure and happy in her environment even through anxiety challenges. Communication with parents is great and I always feel kept “in the loop”.
The whole team at TLC go above and beyond and their different strategies and strengths are the main reason my daughter is a functioning, well developing young person. Also the small community is just so safe for her. I have already recommended several times to different people as I think the school is just so unique.
All the staff are amazing and go above and beyond, not only for my son, but for me as a parent. It hasn’t been an easy start but you have all never given up on him and shown such care, support and encouragement when he has struggled. I couldn’t be prouder of the progress my son has made, passing tests he never thought he would. I don’t say it enough but thank you for everything you do for us both.
The Principal, Helen Dyer is a star. She is very attentive and able to meet my young person’s needs in the moment of difficult behaviours. She always keeps me up to date with what is going wrong and what is going well, and has had a positive impact on my young person.
Staff seem to really love the children they work with and are easy to talk to from both a parent and student perspective.
All staff at TLC are amazing, supportive and go above and beyond.
Where do I start? When we viewed TLC as a possible school we left feeling comfortable and welcomed, you could see how much of a family unit there was within the setting. As time grew on I felt confident that my son was in the right place and would continue to grow.
My son has been at TLC since year 8 and has really excelled since joining the school. Every member of staff has helped him develop into a confident, positive person and student. The small class sizes and number of support staff have been very beneficial in supporting my son achieve what he is capable of in a nurturing environment. He can be himself at TLC and will miss the teachers and his friends when he leaves in Year 11.
We are pleased with L’s progress at TLC. If L had not been accepted at TLC we feel he would not have been able to concentrate on revising and sitting 5 GCSEs. The TLC have enabled L to be able to focus on his schooling rather than him being in competition with his peers as at his previous school.
Despite the odd wobble, Charlie enjoys coming to school. I am confident that he is safe and well looked after. Each teacher and staff member have got to know my son and are really keen to keep him engaged despite his reluctance in some subjects. The support the school offer to Charlie and our family is amazing.
TLC has been amazing with my daughter Emma, very passionate about the kids, very patient, kind and understanding with my daughter’s needs. It’s taken her some time to get her to where she is now but she’s thriving and is content and happy; and it’s all thanks to the wonderful staff at TLC.
Our Son has been going to TLC for three years now. He was in a mainstream school previously which he found overwhelming and struggled to fit in and make friends – he refused to go to school for two years. However, TLC persevered and encouraged Alfie into attending. Since attending, staff have supported him to grow in confidence and blossom as a young man. He now takes part in after school activities and socialises with a group of friends. We are over the moon with our son’s progress and will be eternally grateful to the staff at TLC.
My daughter came to TLC The Learning Centre two terms ago after six years of home education and a stressful time in our lives. Up until then I had spent ten years trying to get her a suitable education but I can say it was worth every minute of waiting and fighting for her to be in this wonderful school.
We have been very impressed with TLC from our very first visit. Even before our daughter was officially a student, she was made to feel incredibly welcome by all of the staff and students. As a student in TLC, she feels accepted and listened to. She is excited to go to school each day in a way that we have never seen before in her previous schools.
My child has grown in confidence since he began at TLC. I worry less about what the future holds for him with his growing confidence and life skills he has learnt during his time at TLC. I wish he could stay on for a few more years, as I know he is safe and most importantly, HAPPY
TLC have been very supportive of our daughter, after years of disrupted education. They have been really understanding and flexible in their approach and have put her needs first at every stage. Staff are kind, understanding and very approachable.
Since my son has started at TLC his whole life has changed, he feels heard at school and safe. He enjoys it that much that his attendance has gone from 36% (mainstream) to over 90% at TLC!

About TLC
Our School
TLC is a small independent Special Educational Needs school in Bromley, Kent. We offer learners a welcoming and secure environment in which to learn and develop as young people.
We provide high-quality education and care for a broad range of complex emotional and academic needs, all of which we aim to support through a nurturing and structured environment which targets learners’ individual needs.
We specialise in young people with:
ASD – Autism Spectrum Disorder
Communication and interaction difficulties
High levels of anxiety
Difficulties in communicating with peers
Depression and self-harm
Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
PTSD – Post traumatic Stress Disorder
Oppositional Defiant Disorder
Signs of abuse and neglect
We offer a range of core therapies to support learners with their learning and developmental needs, including personal mentors, one to one counselling sessions, Speech and Language Therapy and Occupational Therapy. We also have a specialist Dyslexia Teacher and work closely with an educational psychologist.
To provide a holistic approach to supporting our young people, we offer additional activities such as lunch time clubs in music and gaming.
We are trained in Proact SCIPr which is a specialist, pro-active, emotion-informed, behavioural approach, which supports children and young people with challenging behaviour.
We believe every experience is a learning experience and we have a dedicated team who work with each learner to develop a personalised approach to learning and understanding. With the specialist support our learners receive, they grow in self-confidence, personal understanding and develop a more positive approach to learning.
Our Offer
We are proud of the extensive services we provide to our learners and families, which include the following.
Our school’s ethos and aims are to uphold our Purpose, Mission, Vision and Values which are:
Purpose
To ensure all children and young people attending TLC leave us prepared for the world and all that their futures may bring.
Mission
We provide an inspirational, innovative and safe place of education, where each pupil is valued and treated equitably; delivering individualised, high quality educational provision based on the past experiences and current needs of each pupil.
Vision
We will create a school which values inclusivity, provides exceptional educational and personal development opportunities for our pupils, enabling them to overcome barriers, gain self-worth, acquire cultural capital, become independent and ultimately take a meaningful place in society.
Values
This will be delivered through a commitment to Equality & Diversity, Ambition, Inclusion, Valuing People, Integrity, Inspiration, Nurture, Compassion, Pride and Support.
Community and Charity
The school fosters an ethos of charitable work, and we mark nationwide charitable events such as Comic Relief, Children in Need and Macmillan Coffee Mornings.
TLC has partnerships with a number of local charities including Living on Bereavement Living On and Bromley Children & Families Voluntary Sector Forum bcfforum – Voluntary Sector Forum. Living On deliver both 1-2-1 counselling and group drama therapy for our learners who have experienced bereavements. Bromley Children & Families Voluntary Sector Forum work with us to fund and support various projects such as our Summer Transition Days and Youth Mentoring Initiative (funded via the Mayor of London’s Propel funding). We refer Learners to various local charities for additional support on a regular basis including CASPA, Bromley Mencap and Bromley Children’s Project
We work in partnership with Young Lewisham as outlined above to deliver innovative, practical and vocational courses and programmes to our Learners. Further information can be found at YOUNG LEWISHAM PROJECT – Home.
We connect regularly with our local community and our local Councillors; including the Mayor of Bromley.

TLC School Celebrates Learners’ Outstanding GCSE Artwork
TLC School is celebrating the creativity, dedication and artistic talent of its learners following the GCSE Art moderation visit on Tuesday 30th June.
As part of the GCSE assessment process, an external moderator from the examination board visited the school to review learners’ coursework and final pieces. The displayed artwork reflected the considerable time, creativity and commitment learners have invested throughout their Art studies.
Across a wide range of projects, learners demonstrated impressive technical skills, creativity and personal expression, producing work that showcased both their artistic development and individual talents. The exhibition highlighted the breadth and quality of artwork completed during the course and celebrated the dedication learners have shown in developing their creative abilities.
Alex Buck, Head of School at TLC School, said:
“We are incredibly proud of the outstanding artwork our learners have produced. Their creativity, perseverance and commitment have been evident throughout the GCSE Art course, and the quality of work on display reflects the time and effort they have invested. Art provides our learners with a valuable opportunity to express themselves, build confidence and develop important creative skills, and it has been wonderful to see their achievements recognised through the moderation process.”
The GCSE Art exhibition stands as a testament to the hard work of TLC School’s learners and the support of staff who have encouraged them to explore their creativity and reach their full artistic potential.

PSHE and RSE
PSHE
At TLC our PSHE Curriculum is designed with the specific needs of our learners in mind and is reflective of TLC’s aims and ethos. Our ethos focuses on enabling learners to make well informed and positive choices for themselves that lead to them becoming confident young adults who value inclusivity and are prepared for all that their futures may bring. Learners are taught and continually encouraged to respect other people, with particular regard to the protected characteristics set out in the Equality Act 2010. Learners study a different topic every half-term and topics build on one another. For example, learners in Year 7 learn how to use social media safely and in Year 9 how to identify when someone is being groomed online; lessons are age appropriate.
At TLC we understand that PSHE lessons need to be fluid when dealing with topical situations in the lives of our learners, and current affairs that may affect them. We will not hesitate to change the content of lessons should the need arise, for example if a learner has lost a parent we will be sensitive when discussing families, if situations arise in the playground and a learner uses discriminatory language we will use our PSHE lessons to educate learners around this topic. We actively promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs and our Careers curriculum encourages learners to be citizens.
Our PSHE curriculum is planned as per the guidance provided by the DfE and reflects the schools aims and ethos Our objectives are:
For learners to understand and celebrate diversity.
RSE
At The Learning Centre, good relationships are fundamental to our ethos. Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) is lifelong learning about relationships, emotions, looking after ourselves, different families, sex, sexuality and sexual health. It involves acquiring information, developing skills and forming positive beliefs, values and attitudes. RSE has a key part to play in the personal, social, moral and spiritual development of young people.
The aims of relationship and sex education (RSE) at our school are to:
Parents have the right to request children are removed from lessons teaching certain elements of RSE. Information on this can be downloaded here.
Behave responsibly within relationships.

Melrose Education strengthens wellbeing support for learners, families and colleagues
Melrose Education is continuing to strengthen its commitment to wellbeing across its family of specialist schools through the introduction of The Wellbeing Hub, an evidence-based online platform designed to support learners, families and colleagues.
The Wellbeing Hub, developed by Teen Tips, provides a wide range of expert-led resources, including webinars, podcasts, articles, practical guidance and wellbeing advice tailored for staff, parents and young people. The platform takes a proactive approach to mental health and emotional wellbeing, helping school communities build resilience, strengthen relationships and access trusted support whenever they need it.
Across Melrose Education, Wellbeing Champions are using the platform to signpost colleagues and families to high-quality resources, helping to promote positive wellbeing both in school and at home. By supporting the whole school community, the initiative reflects Melrose Education’s belief that the best outcomes for learners are achieved when families, colleagues and schools work together.
Tracey Storey, Founder, Executive Chair and CEO of Melrose Education, said:
“At Melrose Education, we know that wellbeing is fundamental to learning, development and success. By providing our Wellbeing Champions, colleagues and families with access to The Wellbeing Hub, we are investing in a proactive approach that supports our whole school communities. When learners, families and staff feel supported, connected and equipped with the right tools, everyone benefits.”
The introduction of The Wellbeing Hub forms part of Melrose Education’s wider commitment to creating positive, inclusive environments where learners can thrive academically, socially and emotionally, while ensuring families and colleagues have access to practical, evidence-based wellbeing support whenever they need it.

Curriculum
Our Curriculum Offer
We have a fully inclusive curriculum which allows all learners to achieve and feel success. We cover a broad range of subjects that enhance the skills, knowledge and understanding of our young people. We have a particular focus on learners’ understanding of the world around them, so that they can implement what they learn into everyday life.
​We strongly believe that all students are capable of gaining qualifications that allow them to move on to the next stage of life with an element of choice in what they do next. This prepares learners to leave the nurturing environment of TLC and live, work and play, in the wider world.
We believe that our curriculum enables students to:
have the essential functional skills of Maths, English and Science.
have enquiring minds and think for themselves.
integrate into society and interact with the people around them in a meaningful way.
build a sense of self-worth and self-confidence and develop a positive self-image.
form positive relationships with their peers
Our curriculum provides a rich and broad education that is coherently planned and sequenced so that new knowledge and skills are built on.
Through this varied and differentiated curriculum we aim to improve learner motivation, self-confidence, attendance and engagement, whilst equipping young people with the knowledge and cultural capital they need to succeed in life.
At TLC, we teach young people in small classes of between 5 and 10 learners to ensure the personalised needs of each young person are met.
The core subjects of mathematics, English and computing are supplemented by a range of vocational and other academic subjects, to enable the delivery of a broad, rich curriculum. Additional subjects taught include:
P.E. (Active Afternoon)
Employability and Careers
Reading
At TLC, we aim to develop confident readers who enjoy a wide range of texts and are motivated to improve their skills. We promote a love of reading across the whole school and curriculum. Reading is embedded across the curriculum and guided by the latest gov.uk guidance.
We focus on two key elements:
These are grounded in research and supported by the Education Endowment Foundation’s Reading Comprehension House framework. Our reading strategy helps learners develop strong communication skills for education and beyond.
Word Reading: building decoding skills
Vocational Pathways and Work Experience
Key Stage 3 and 4 learners undertake Careers and Citizenship studies to help them with their Personal Development. At Key Stage 3 and 4 ASDAN short course qualifications are embedded within the curriculum, these courses develop skills across a range of topics and curriculum areas. The skills, knowledge and understanding gained during these courses help learners prepare for work. They are offered on an options basis so learners have the freedom and integrity to make their own choices around subjects that interest them.
All learners will study the LiFE, Lessons in Financial Education, course run by the London Institute of Banking and Finance. This online based study course teaches learners about the importance of managing money. Learners work online at their own pace and can gain topic based certificates all the way to a Level 2 qualification.
These additional curriculum choices and qualifications aim to give learners a solid base to further develop their individual skills and interests. ASDAN short course offers include:
Animal Care Short Course
FoodWise Short Course
Land-Based Studies Short Course
Football Short Course
Hair and Beauty Short Course
Outreach Programme
At TLC we have a strong relationship with The Young Lewisham Project, a charity that helps young learners. In Key Stage 4, learners can attend day release placements. The Young Lewisham Project also come into TLC to work with KS3 students and this forms part of their timetabled curriculum. They offer the following programmes of study:
Our Work Experience Programme is developing, and we currently offer internal work experience where learners work in the school office and undertake other roles and work-shadowing around the school to build up their confidence. We are working with organisations and businesses in the local community to develop supported work experience initiatives and experiences for our Learners in years 10-12.
Bike and Car Mechanics
Expressive Arts
Gardening and Horticulture
DJ and Music Technology

SEND
SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities) at TLC The Learning Centre
At TLC The Learning Centre, our ethos is based upon full inclusion, high expectations, exceptional teaching and learning, nurture, and a relentless focus on the needs and potential of every child. We believe it is our duty to provide equal opportunities for every young person in our care in a safe and fully equipped learning environment, which caters to the needs of every student as an individual.
Our vision is to create a school which values inclusivity and provides exceptional educational and personal development opportunities for our learners. This encourages individual qualities and enables our learners to gain self-worth, become independent, acquire cultural capital and ultimately take a meaningful and fulfilling place in society.
At TLC The Learning Centre, all of our learners have an Education Health and Care Plan (EHCP). We are a mixed SEN profile school and as such provide for the 4 main categories of Special Educational Needs as noted in the SEN Code of Practice 2022; Communication and Interaction, Cognition and Learning, Social, Mental and Emotional Health Difficulties and Sensory and/or Physical Needs.
We have a team of Learning Support Assistants who work alongside the teaching staff at TLC and are assigned to key groups of learners and offer support in lessons. Our team also run small group interventions to ensure the EHCP provisions of the learner are met. We offer on-site support from Speech and Language Therapists, Counsellors, Occupational Therapists, Educational Psychologists and Specialist SEN teachers.
We follow the work of Trauma Informed experts and offer a ‘Team around the child’ approach which sees learners having access to a couple of key trusted adults to maximize their chance of feeling safe and nurtured at school. This is further enhanced by the PROACT-SCIPr-UK® approach which we have adopted to develop our intervention, prevention and crisis strategies.
We have robust systems in place to ensure learners, parents/carers and outside agencies are all involved in the process of educating our students during their time here at TLC. We have a specific approach to ‘Quality First Teaching’ and adapt our curriculum to ensure the bespoke needs of our learners are being met, whilst having secure review and evaluation structures in place. Further information about this and Bromley’s Local Offer, can be found in our SEN Information Report.
Our SENDCo leads on, and completes the necessary paperwork for the annual review cycle for EHCP’s and learners are involved in the Annual SEND Review meeting so they can provide feedback on their education and progress. Regular contact and discussions take place between home and school, and learner check-ins take place on a daily basis.

TLC School Celebrates Year 11 and Year 12 Leavers
Learners, families and staff at TLC School came together on Friday 19th June to celebrate the achievements of the school’s Year 11 and Year 12 learners as they marked the end of an important chapter in their educational journey.
Following the completion of their GCSE examinations, learners were joined by parents and carers for a special leavers’ celebration, recognising the hard work, resilience and determination they have demonstrated throughout their time at TLC School.
As part of the event, each learner was presented with a commemorative leavers’ hoodie and a gift card to mark the occasion and celebrate their achievements. The afternoon provided an opportunity for learners, families and staff to reflect on their successes and look ahead with excitement to the next stage of their education.
Learners will return to TLC School on Thursday 20th August for GCSE Results Day before beginning their transitions into new schools, colleges and further education opportunities.
Alex Buck, Head of School at TLC School, said:
“We are incredibly proud of everything our Year 11 and Year 12 learners have achieved during their time at TLC School. They have shown resilience, determination and tremendous personal growth, particularly throughout their GCSE examinations. It was wonderful to celebrate this important milestone alongside their families, and we wish every learner the very best as they move on to the next stage of their education. We look forward to welcoming them back on Results Day to celebrate their achievements once again.”
Everyone at TLC School wishes the departing learners every success for the future and looks forward to hearing about the exciting opportunities that lie ahead.

Careers & Post 16
Careers & Post 16
At The Learning Centre, careers education, information, advice and guidance is a priority for ensuring learners move forward with the right tools and attitude to help prepare them for their future. Our varied and inclusive curriculum supports learners to consider their future options, realise their potential, be able to identify their skills, and transfer them to further education and the job market. Our dedicated Careers Lead at TLC The Learning Centre is Alex Buck.
We ensure that learners are motivated and excited for the world of work. We strive for high levels of expectations around self-confidence, emotional confidence and aspirations that are underpinned by our inclusive, tailored and robust PSHE curriculum and our continued work around the Zones of Regulation.
We prepare learners, and liaise with parents and carers, for their preferred Post 16 pathway whether that is to continue with further education, training or employment. We are fully committed to our statutory and moral obligation to provide a structured, varied and personalised careers education to all Key Stage 3 and Key Stage 4 learners.
Our Year 11 learners have a range of opportunities for their Post 16 options. Some choose to continue their education and TLC, and some move on to local colleges or take apprenticeships.
Our careers curriculum is planned as per the guidance provided by the Gatsby Benchmark and DfE Guidance. Our objectives are:
We are committed to ensuring that wherever possible all learners are in education, employment or training post 16 and avoid becoming NEET (Not in Employment, Education, or Training).
Post 16 Transition Timeline
At TLC we are committed to ensuring that Year 11 learners move on to the appropriate Post 16 environment, be that; college, apprenticeship or training. Our robust Post 16 transition timeline means we continuously communicate with learners, parents and carers to ensure a smooth transition into an appropriate environment; this is underpinned by our Careers lesson which are written to the guidance of the 8 Gatsby Benchmarks. We aim to ensure that no learner becomes NEET.

Wellbeing and Mental Health
Wellbeing and Mental Health at TLC The Learning Centre
We are committed to providing all our learners with rich and diverse experiences which promote their wellbeing, as well as their personal and social development.
We know that in order to secure positive outcomes for our learners, promoting and prioritising positive mental health is essential.
We are proud to work with experienced Speech and Language and Occupational Therapists who work on site two days per week. We also have a qualified Counsellor who offers 1:1 counselling sessions to ensure the maximum positive impact on learner’s emotional wellbeing and resilience. Our Counsellor also offers a ‘drop-in’ service for those who feel the need to talk occasionally, or who are unsure about whether counselling is for them.
We have a school Wellbeing Champion who is there to support our staff team. Our Wellbeing Champion manages a number of initiatives designed to promote a healthy and proactive environment, and to create a sense of community and belonging. Our Principal, Helen Dyer is the school’s Senior Mental Health Lead. She is certified by Trauma Informed Schools and is a trained Mental Health First Aider. A number of other staff members are also Mental Health First Aid trained.
We have access to Melrose Education’s ‘we are listening’ email address, and take part in staff wellbeing sessions and wellbeing surveys.
We can, and do, make referrals to many local services for our families to access support, including frequently to Bromley Y and Bromley Children’s Project.

YoungMinds offers free confidential online and telephone support to anyone worried about the emotional and mental wellbeing of a child or young person up to the age of 25.
MindEd for Families
MindEd for families is a branch of MindEd, intended to support parents and those caring for children and young people.
MindEd is an online e-portal offering free, simple advice about children and young people’s mental health for all adults.

Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) – Bromley
Bromley Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service (BrCAMHS) supports people under the age of 18 who are struggling with their mental health.
They provide routine and urgent assessments and perform evidence-based interventions based on the individual’s clinical needs. These interventions include providing advice, signposting and brief focused, goal-based support.
They provide early intervention services through children’s centres and schools across the borough of Bromley.
Please note they are not an emergency service.
